problem:
The mass $M(t),$ in micrograms, of a sample of potassium-42 is given by

$$
M(t)=30{e}^{-kt},
$$

where $t$ is the time, in hours. The half-life of potassium-42 is $12.36\,\text{h}.$ Rounded to three significant figures, what is the value of $k?$
worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

Since we know that ${t}_{1/2}=12.36\,\text{h}$ we have

$$
12.36=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}\,⇒\,k=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{12.36}≈0.0561
$$
